notes: C runtime functions under the System V x86-64 convention (args RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX; result RAX). Preserved: RBX, RBP, R12-R15. Every entry is a declared assumption.

entries.name: memcpy
entries.notes: dst[0, n) = src[0, n); returns dst. Exact only when n is proven constant at the call.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (glibc manual: Copying Strings and Arrays); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: memset
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (glibc manual); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strcpy
entries.notes: For a defined call (src NUL-terminated, dst writable and large enough, no overlap -- otherwise undefined behaviour): dst[0] = src[0] when it returns (strcpy copies at least the terminating NUL, src[0] first); the rest has an extent known only at run time: all other memory is unknown. Returns dst.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (glibc manual); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strcat
entries.notes: Writes an extent known only at run time (strncpy with n == 0 writes nothing; strcat writes after dst's string): no memory is kept. Returns dst.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (glibc manual); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: longjmp
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.13.2.1, _Noreturn): only the paths after the call end; the setjmp side is not modeled here (an opaque call). Reads the jmp_buf rdi points to (observes rdi).

registered: pthread cancellation cleanup handlers of the frames left (glibc _longjmp_unwind)

entries.callbacks_evidence: glibc setjmp/longjmp.c (_longjmp_unwind); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: __stack_chk_fail
entries.notes: glibc's stack-protector failure: never returns (declared noreturn); uses no pointer it receives.
entries.callbacks_evidence: glibc debug/stack_chk_fail.c -> __fortify_fail -> abort (raises SIGABRT); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: abort
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.22.4.1): the paths through it end there. Uses no pointer it receives (observes nothing).
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.22.4.1; glibc stdlib/abort.c (raises SIGABRT); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strlen
entries.notes: Reads memory of unknown extent: the result is left unknown; memory unchanged.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (glibc manual); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: malloc
entries.notes: Returns a new block's address (no program data flows into it; fresh: never an address of memory existing before the call, the stack included). Heap bookkeeping is not program-visible memory (assumption).
entries.callbacks_evidence: glibc manual: Hooks for Malloc (removed in 2.34); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: free
entries.notes: Assumes no use after free: the freed block's contents are not read again. Uses no pointer it receives on program-visible memory and keeps none (observes nothing).
entries.callbacks_evidence: glibc manual: Hooks for Malloc; free releases its argument's block; audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: realloc
entries.notes: Returns a block holding the old contents: the same object as the old pointer, assuming the old pointer is not used afterwards (no-use-of-old-pointer-after-realloc); realloc(NULL, n) is a fresh block.
entries.callbacks_evidence: glibc manual: Hooks for Malloc; realloc may free / move the old block; audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)
